verifyReport.summary: Interactive prompting and logger creation are expanded across terminal and browser environments, with terminal-specific prompt and output utilities added.
keyChanges: Logger instances now support interactive text, confirmation, single-choice, and multiple-choice prompts, and the example starts these questions automatically when run.
Browser prompts use native dialogs: confirmations use a yes-or-no dialog, while text, single-choice, and multiple-choice prompts use a text dialog and do not present supplied choices.

Logger creation now has platform-specific defaults and accepts caller-supplied reporters; the browser entry point also reuses an existing global logger, and the shared export surface no longer provides logger creation.

Terminal prompt output now includes text, password, confirmation, single-choice, multiple-choice, grouped-choice, status-symbol, and display helpers; multiple-choice selection can allow an empty result, and symbols have a non-Unicode fallback.

checks: Verify the example begins asking questions automatically and the text question shows the initial value java and placeholder Not sure.
Confirm the confirmation question accepts either yes or no and then proceeds to the next question.
Check the single-choice question shows both TypeScript entries and the CoffeeScript entry, including its supplied hint, and allows choosing an entry.
Verify the optional multiple-choice question can be submitted with no tools selected and completes with an empty selection.
Verify a confirmation prompt opens a native confirmation dialog and returns the chosen yes-or-no result.
Check a text prompt opens a native text dialog and a select or multiple-choice prompt also opens a native text dialog rather than showing its supplied choices.
Confirm logger creation is available from platform-specific package entry points and is not available through the shared export surface.
Verify default logging uses the regular-runtime reporter outside CI and test environments, and the basic reporter in CI or test environments.
Check that creating a logger with an explicitly empty reporter list does not fall back to a default reporter when a message is logged.
Confirm the browser entry point reuses an existing global logger rather than replacing it.
Verify a password question masks entered characters, and a terminal without Unicode support uses fallback symbols for prompt states.

Check a grouped multiple-choice question keeps group labels and entries distinguishable, and pressing Enter with no selection when selection is required displays the message Please select at least one option.
Confirm a note containing multiline text with ANSI-colored characters still renders its text within an aligned box.
Verify multiline status messages show subsequent lines separately and a spinner started with Loading... displays Loading without the trailing dots while active.

uncertainty: No application navigation or account context was supplied, so these checks must be reached through the supplied example or package capabilities rather than an identified application screen.

baseChecks: Verify a text prompt configured with initial value java and placeholder Not sure shows those values and accepts a typed response.
Confirm a confirmation prompt initialized to true starts on the affirmative choice and returns the user's chosen true or false value.
Check a single-select prompt with string choices and a labeled choice with a hint displays the choices and hint and returns the selected value.
Ensure a multi-select prompt configured with required false accepts Enter with no options selected and returns an empty selection.
Verify logger creation in CI or test mode uses basic console reporting, while a regular non-CI runtime uses fancy console reporting.
Check logger creation with reporters set to [] does not substitute the default reporter, and confirm subsequent log calls produce no reporter output.

verifyReport.summary: This release changes how drawings are restored and how selection and pasted elements are handled, with the greatest QA focus on loading saved scenes safely.
keyChanges: Loading invalid JSON now catches the parsing error and returns an empty scene, whereas previously parsing was not caught and the existing drawing was not replaced through this load path.
Shift-clicking blank canvas now retains the existing selection, whereas previously clicking blank canvas cleared it regardless of Shift.
Pasting elements no longer subtracts the source group's minimum x and y coordinates from their placement, so a group whose minimum coordinates are nonzero is positioned by that additional offset.

checks: Verify loading the invalid JSON file results in an empty canvas, rather than leaving the existing drawing in place.
Confirm that Shift-clicking the blank area retains the element selection, while clicking the same area without Shift clears it.
Check that the pasted element appears 100 units farther horizontally and 50 units farther vertically than it would with the previous source-origin adjustment.

uncertainty: Whether replacing the current drawing with an empty canvas after loading invalid JSON is intended remains unclear.

baseChecks: Verify loading the JSON file without an elements field replaces the visible drawing with a blank scene.
Check that Shift-clicking blank canvas leaves the existing element selected.
Verify that pasting the copied group applies the same calculated x and y offset to its elements without first subtracting the group’s minimum x and y coordinates.

verifyReport.summary: The release reorganizes URL and query handling, replacing the previous URL interface and changing how some URL and query inputs are parsed and serialized.
keyChanges: The new URL capability separates protocol, host, authentication, path, query, and fragment handling, and provides URL details such as hostname, port, username, password, origin, full path, and href.
Protocol recognition now requires a scheme matching letters, digits, or underscores before ://; a URL beginning web+demo:// is handled as a path by the new parser.
Query parsing ignores entries with an empty key and combines repeated non-empty keys into multiple values; query updates and serialization use the new query representation.

The old URL interface and parameter helpers are removed from the public exports, while the new URL and query capabilities are exported; query encoding emits a bare key for a missing or empty value and repeated key-value pairs for arrays.

checks: Verify that web+demo://example.com/a is handled as a path rather than as a URL with a protocol.

Check that https://user:pass@example.com/path?x=1#part exposes the host, username, password, path, query, fragment, origin, full path, and href consistently, and that string and JSON serialization return the href.
Confirm that a relative URL remains a relative href, and that appending a relative URL combines its path, adds its query values, and applies its fragment.
Verify that parsing ?=value&item=one&item=two ignores the empty key and returns both values for item.
Check that updating a URL preserves existing query entries not replaced by the update, omits the equals sign for missing and empty values, and serializes array values as repeated key-value pairs.
Confirm that the public entry point exposes the new URL and query capabilities and parse and utility exports, without relying on the removed URL interface or parameter helpers.

uncertainty: The removed-code evidence does not show the prior protocol-detection rule, so it cannot establish whether web+demo:// was treated differently before this release.

baseChecks: Verify that parsing and serializing ?=x omits the empty-key parameter from the resulting URL.
Check that parsing guide?x=1 without a protocol returns pathname guide and search x=1.
Confirm that the package entry point exposes the URL, query, and encoding utility exports in place of the previous UFO module export.

verifyReport.summary: Library handling is being separated from scene updates and centralized across imports, shared links, and the embeddable editor.
keyChanges: Library items supplied with scene data are now handled separately: startup data and refreshed stored items update the library directly, while scene updates continue to update the drawing.

Library file selection now uses a different chooser path, and cancellation is handled quietly; dropped library files merge with existing items and open the library, while shared-library links merge published items and open the library.
The embeddable editor exposes library handling through its public integration API, and its example now distinguishes drawing files from library files and displays pointer coordinates.

testAreas.area: Library startup, file import, and drop
checks: Verify startup with initial drawing data containing a library item preserves that item alongside the existing library rather than replacing existing items.
Check that choosing a valid library file through the library file chooser adds its item to the library, and that cancelling the chooser leaves the library unchanged without an import error.
Confirm dropping a valid library file merges its item with the existing library item and opens the library.
Confirm opening a shared-library link adds linked items without removing existing items, opens the library, and restores the prior address after import.
Verify a link with no matching editor token prompts for confirmation before adding its items, while a link with a matching token adds them without that prompt.
Verify loading a drawing file updates the drawing, while loading a library file adds its items to the library and opens the library rather than replacing the drawing.

Check that an integration update containing library items is handled through the separate library-update capability, and that the items appear in the library; use a legacy-format library item list as input if available.

Confirm the example's scene updates, image loading, clipboard copy, and export still operate, and that pointer movement updates the displayed x and y coordinates and comment interactions remain usable.

uncertainty: The supplied chooser change shows the file-opening call and cancellation handling but does not show the selected file being passed to library import; verify that choosing a valid library file still adds its items.

baseChecks: Verify that opening a shared-library link in the legacy query-string form with a matching editor token imports the items without a confirmation prompt, preserves existing items, opens the Library, and removes the import link from the address.
Check that selecting a valid library file through the Library load control adds its items while preserving an existing item.
Confirm that a Library update requested to merge valid items adds them without replacing existing items.
Verify that a Library update requested to open the Library makes it visible.

verifyReport.summary: URL parsing and formatting behavior has been replaced, changing how URL inputs and query parameters are handled.
keyChanges: Repeated query keys are now retained as ordered values instead of only keeping the last value, allowing URL formatting to preserve repetitions.
URL parameter values now encode slashes as %2F, and URL construction rejects non-string inputs that the previous parser accepted as parsed URL objects.

uncertainty: Whether rejecting parsed URL objects is an intended compatibility change is not documented in the supplied context.

verifyReport.summary: The release adds an on-demand statistics panel for drawings and selected elements, with supporting selection and storage updates.
keyChanges: A new stats panel opens from the canvas context menu, displays scene and selected-element information, and can be closed from the panel.
Storage figures are collected after a 500 ms debounce; the total includes stored app state, collaboration data, library data, and scene elements, and closing the panel cancels its pending refresh.
Selected-shape controls and the stats panel now use plural target resolution, so property changes and displayed selected-element details can account for multiple targets.
Clearing a drawing now preserves whether the stats panel is open or closed.
The existing selection-membership and filtered-selection calculations have no evidenced change in behavior.

checks: Verify the canvas context menu provides a stats entry; choose it and confirm the panel appears, then use its close control and confirm it hides.

Check that a scene containing exactly two elements displays an element count of 2 and scene dimensions; with both elements selected, confirm the panel shows a selected-element count of 2 and the combined position and dimensions.
Confirm the panel shows scene and total storage figures after the delayed refresh, and that the total reflects stored app state, collaboration data, library data, and scene elements.
Test opening and immediately closing the panel before 500 ms elapses; confirm it stays closed, then reopen it and confirm storage figures appear.
Test changing sharpness with exactly two elements selected and confirm both selected elements receive the change.
Confirm selecting and deselecting an element continues to update which elements are selected, without changing the existing selection-membership behavior.

baseChecks: Verify the statistics entry opens the panel and its close control dismisses it.

Check that with two elements in the scene and both selected, the panel shows the scene count, rounded scene dimensions, selected-element count of 2, and rounded position and dimensions for the combined selection.
Confirm that selecting exactly one rotated element shows its position, rounded dimensions, and angle in degrees, while the multiple-selection section is absent.
Validate that scene and total storage sizes appear as compact values after they load.
Test changing sharpness with exactly two selected elements and confirm the selection-based control remains available and applies the chosen value to both elements.

verifyReport.summary: The release adds a keyboard-toggleable Zen mode and updates how editor controls and edge panels are presented.
keyChanges: Zen mode starts off and can be toggled with Alt+Z or exited from a new footer control; editor panels and the lock control also receive Zen-mode-specific presentation changes.
Edge-anchored editor panels now support additional styling, and floating tool surfaces use the updated styling bundle, affecting their presentation in the editor and mobile menu.
Tool controls now use a changed visibility-class mapping, so their displayed state needs verification when controls are available or unavailable.

checks: Verify that pressing Alt+Z with no Ctrl or Command modifier turns Zen mode on, and pressing Alt+Z again turns it off; confirm the shortcut is listed in the shortcuts dialog.

verifyReport.summary: The release changes how consumers receive the logger and makes legacy compatibility operations available.
keyChanges: The default package export changes from the logger class to an initialized logger instance, while the class and factory are available as named exports.
Previously inactive compatibility operations for reporter management, scoping, mocking, and pausing or resuming logs are now available at runtime.

testAreas.area: Package logger entry point and compatibility operations
checks: Verify that the default package export is a ready-to-use logger instance and that the named class can be constructed and the named factory can create a logger.
Check that the legacy reporter-add compatibility call registers the prepared reporter so it receives a log message; previously that compatibility call was inactive.

baseChecks: Verify a consumer using the package default export receives the shared logger instance and can still construct a logger through the named Consola export.
Check that a logger instance’s legacy add alias accepts a reporter and adds it, rather than being unavailable.
Confirm that Types remains available as a named export and that reporter constructors are not forwarded through the main package entry point.

verifyReport.summary: The release updates text creation and drawing-property controls, including how edited and selected elements supply displayed values.
keyChanges: Drawing-property controls now prefer the actively edited element’s value, otherwise using a shared selected-element value or a default; mixed values have no single shared value, and opacity 0 falls through to the 100 default.

When no color is set, the color chooser now receives an explicit null value instead of an undefined value; the chooser continues to serve canvas background, element background, and stroke color controls.
Text elements are measured and positioned when created or submitted, and submitting empty text no longer adds an element to the drawing.

testAreas.area: Drawing appearance controls and color chooser
checks: Verify that an element with stored opacity 0 displays 100 in the opacity control under the new default behavior.

Check that while editing a text element whose appearance differs from other selected elements, the controls show the edited element’s values; for multiple selected elements with different stroke widths, confirm the control does not present a single shared width.
Confirm that with no color set, opening a canvas background or element color chooser and selecting a palette color visibly applies that color to the corresponding background or stroke.
Verify that submitting empty text creates no text element in the drawing.
Confirm that submitting non-empty text creates a text element with the entered text visible and its size fitted to that text.

uncertainty: A stored opacity of 0 now falls through to the default of 100 in the control; whether fully transparent elements should continue to display 0 is unclear.

baseChecks: Verify an element with opacity 0 is selected and the opacity control displays 100 under the new fallback.
Check that while editing a text element with different appearance settings from another selected element, the controls show the edited text element’s values.
Verify that submitting an empty string does not add a new empty text item.
Check that submitting non-empty text updates or creates the text item with bounds matching the entered text and font.
